description: Instrument the Mohist server to emit its own OpenTelemetry traces for the inbound HTTP -> SignalR -> Orleans -> EF Core -> outbound HttpClient execution chain, export them via OTLP HTTP to a configurable endpoint (default the #219 same-process collector), exclude the /otel/ path to prevent self-feedback, degrade silently on exporter failure, and be fully disableable via a master switch.

tasks.title: Add OtelOptions, master-switch-gated OTel SDK host registration, OTLP HTTP exporter, inbound HTTP source with /otel/ filter, and exporter-failure isolation
tasks.description: Add the OtelOptions config class (Mohist:Otel section, Enabled default true, Endpoint default http://localhost:4318/otel) and the AddMohistOpenTelemetry(IServiceCollection, IConfiguration) extension in Infrastructure/Hosting, called from ConfigureMohistServices. The extension gates the entire AddOpenTelemetry() call on OtelOptions.Enabled: when off it registers nothing. When on, it builds one TracerProvider with ConfigureResource(AddService("Mohist.Server")), AddAspNetCoreInstrumentation with a Filter that excludes the /otel/ path prefix (self-feedback guard), and UseOtlpExporter configured for HttpProtobuf at the configured endpoint. Add the required NuGet references. Exporter failure isolation relies on the SDK's BatchExportProcessor; verify by test, no defensive try/catch.
acceptanceCriteria: OtelOptions binds from the Mohist:Otel section; Enabled defaults to true and Endpoint defaults to http://localhost:4318/otel. A unit test verifies both defaults and that MOHIST__Otel__Endpoint overrides the config-file value.

AddMohistOpenTelemetry is invoked from ConfigureMohistServices and, when Enabled == false, does NOT call AddOpenTelemetry() — a test using an in-memory Activity-capturing processor asserts zero spans are collected and no OTel hosted service is registered.

When enabled, an inbound HTTP request to a mapped route produces exactly one ASP.NET Core inbound span carrying the matched route template and the final HTTP response status code (in-memory exporter test).

An inbound request whose path starts with /otel (e.g. POST /otel/v1/traces) produces NO inbound span — the Filter predicate returns false for that path (in-memory exporter test asserts empty capture).

The OTLP exporter is configured with OtlpExportProtocol.HttpProtobuf and the Endpoint from OtelOptions; a test asserts the exporter options carry the configured protocol and endpoint, and that the export pipeline delivers spans (verified by registering an in-memory capturing processor that records the spans the processor would export).

With the endpoint pointed at an unreachable port (connection refused), the server starts, serves a sample request without throwing, and the request is not delayed beyond the exporter's own bounded timeout — integration test asserts no exception and no request-path blocking.

Mohist.Server.csproj references OpenTelemetry.Extensions.Hosting, OpenTelemetry.Exporter.OpenTelemetryProtocol, and OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.AspNetCore; dotnet build passes with TreatWarningsAsErrors.
Existing server tests pass unchanged (zero regression): npm test at packages/server is green and no test opts into tracing unless it explicitly enables it.
tasks.output: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Infrastructure/Config/OtelOptions.cs, packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Infrastructure/Hosting/MohistOpenTelemetryRegistration.cs, updated MohistServiceRegistration.cs and Mohist.Server.csproj, accompanying unit + integration tests
tasks.notes: Also satisfies the spec requirements 'Traces are exported over OTLP HTTP to a configurable endpoint', 'Exporter failure is non-fatal', 'Instrumentation can be fully disabled with a master switch', and the trace-only/no-logs-no-metrics portion of 'Only automatic, trace-only instrumentation'. Implementation MUST follow design Decisions 1, 2, 4, and 5. The test fixture (ConfigureMohistServices is shared per its doc-comment) must not regress; existing tests that do not set Mohist:Otel stay unaffected. The OTLP exporter appends /v1/traces to the configured endpoint, so http://localhost:4318/otel resolves to #219's POST /otel/v1/traces route — confirm against #219's routing once both changes share a branch.

tasks.title: Complete the five-segment execution chain: add SignalR, Orleans, EF Core, and outbound HttpClient sources and prove single-trace continuity
tasks.spec: specs/server-otel-tracing/spec.md#Traces form one unbroken execution chain across all segments
tasks.description: Extend the WithTracing block from T-001 to subscribe the remaining four sources: AddSource("Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Server") (built-in .NET 10+), AddSource for the Orleans native ActivitySource (confirm exact name(s) emitted by Orleans 10 by capturing all source names during a sample grain call), AddHttpClientInstrumentation(), and AddEntityFrameworkCoreInstrumentation() from the contrib package. Add the EF Core and HttpClient instrumentation NuGet references. All sources share the single TracerProvider so they propagate the ambient Activity.Current and attach as parent-child along the real execution path. Verify no self-feedback outbound span leaks from the exporter's own OTLP POST; if any leaks, apply the HttpClientInstrumentationOptions.FilterHttpRequestMessage fallback from design Decision 4.
acceptanceCriteria: The WithTracing block subscribes Microsoft.AspNetCore.SignalR.Server, the confirmed Orleans ActivitySource name(s), EF Core instrumentation, and HttpClient instrumentation, all on the single TracerProvider established in T-001.

The exact Orleans ActivitySource name(s) are confirmed empirically by sending one grain call through the instrumented host and recording every emitted source name; the subscribed name(s) match what Orleans 10 actually emits (documented in the test).

A SignalR hub method invocation produces one hub-method span whose parent is the active activity context of the carrying connection — child of the inbound request that established the interaction (in-memory exporter test).
An Orleans grain call triggered by a hub or request produces a grain-invocation span that is a child of the calling activity context, making the grain chain observable within the same trace (test).
An EF Core query issued inside a grain produces a deeper child span carrying the SQL text as an attribute and the query duration (test).
An outbound HttpClient call (e.g. readiness probe or self-update check) produces a child span carrying the destination URI and response status code (test).

A single end-to-end request flowing inbound HTTP -> SignalR hub -> Orleans grain -> EF Core query -> outbound HttpClient yields all spans under one shared trace id, each non-root span carrying the correct parent span id of its causal caller, with no orphan spans — integration test using the in-memory exporter from T-001.

No outbound HttpClient span appears whose destination is the configured OTLP endpoint (exporter self-feedback verification); if any such span leaks, the FilterHttpRequestMessage fallback from design Decision 4 is applied and this test passes.

dotnet build passes with TreatWarningsAsErrors (Mohist.Server.csproj now also references OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.Http and OpenTelemetry.Instrumentation.EntityFrameworkCore); npm test at packages/server is green.
tasks.output: updated MohistOpenTelemetryRegistration.cs (four additional sources), updated Mohist.Server.csproj (two additional instrumentation packages), integration tests proving single-trace continuity and self-feedback absence
tasks.notes: Also satisfies spec requirements 'SignalR hub method invocations are traced as child spans', 'Orleans grain calls are traced as child spans', 'EF Core database queries are traced with SQL text', 'Outbound HttpClient calls are traced', and the 'no custom business spans' portion of 'Only automatic, trace-only instrumentation'. Implementation MUST follow design Decisions 3 (single provider, sources added to the same block), the Orleans source-name mitigation in Risks, and the outbound suppression verification in Open Questions. Trace continuity is a property of subscribing all five sources to one provider that shares Activity.Current — no custom propagation code is written.
